reference.evidence: Encoded film stills, visually inspected. No proposed lighting change has been rendered or approved.

existingRig.units: Unreal centimeters; intensity numbers are source values, not measured illuminance
existingRig.note: The source does not explicitly configure a sky cubemap here. Inspect actual sky contribution before relying on it. This records source settings, not measured light output.

findings.title: Input pallet side faces
findings.observation: Brick tops read well; lower side faces, pallet support and pickup clearance are less readable beneath the heads.
findings.proposal: Retain the existing input fill. Trial a broad neutral side bounce aimed across lower stack faces; avoid adding more overhead light to already bright tops.
findings.anchor: input cart bounds and top-layer pickup envelope
findings.acceptance: The bottom pallet edge and head-to-stack clearance remain visible without washing out the warm brick surfaces.

findings.title: Dehacking head separation
findings.observation: Pickup faces are readable, while dark vertical rods and beam undersides merge into the surrounding gantry.
findings.proposal: Trial a restrained broad rear/side edge light on the head bank, plus soft underside fill where needed. Preserve depth and avoid reflective hotspots on the stack tops.
findings.acceptance: Head silhouettes and vertical travel separate from the gantry throughout the layer lift.

findings.title: Row transfer and receiving subbelt
findings.observation: The row is visible, but dark receiving-belt edges, supports and adjacent gripper parts offer weak separation. The cyan receiving surface draws disproportionate attention.
findings.proposal: Rebalance the existing profile fill toward row side faces and the receiving edge. Trial a soft opposite-side edge light on the gripper. Keep the physical-video matching profile camera fixed.
findings.acceptance: Pickup, clearance and placement can be read in the fixed profile without lifting the whole frame or creating a cyan hotspot.

findings.title: Inspection head and reject junction
findings.observation: White light bars and silver rollers dominate. The dark head/support assembly has less visual definition, weakening the inspection-system hierarchy.
findings.proposal: Trial broad neutral side fill and a restrained edge light on the sensor housing. Balance bright bar surfaces after checking material/emission and exposure; retain readable brick color and the opaque reject belt.
findings.anchor: inspection portal, sensing footprint and reject junction
findings.acceptance: Housing, sensing area and reject branch are distinguishable during the seven-second hold; bright bars retain useful shape and do not obscure the bricks.

findings.title: Brick visibility across routing tables
findings.observation: Repeated bright roller highlights compete with small bricks; some brick side faces are dark relative to the transport surface.
findings.proposal: Trial soft cross-light grazing the brick side faces and rebalance key-light direction. Inspect roller roughness only if highlights still dominate after lighting changes; do not recolor the tracked brick.
findings.anchor: active routing tables and brick travel height
findings.acceptance: The tracked brick stays distinguishable at 1080p without changing its material identity or the process geometry.

findings.title: Pallet formation inside the frame
findings.observation: The forming stack is substantially darker than the exposed roller decks; frame bars overlap its front face.
findings.proposal: Trial a low broad side fill into the well and a subtle rear edge light. Keep genuine contact shading. Structural occlusion is a separate camera-composition issue and cannot be solved with light alone.
findings.acceptance: Successive layers remain legible during continuous accelerated formation without making the frame disappear or lighting the brick from within.

findings.title: Pallet face inside the bridge gripper
findings.observation: The yellow gripper top is prominent while the pallet face inside its opening is deeply shaded. Similar loss persists during the bridge journey.
findings.proposal: Trial broad side lighting covering the bridge travel envelope from both oblique directions. Balance the yellow top separately from the pallet face. Prefer stationary area lights over a camera-mounted spotlight.
findings.acceptance: The carried pallet face and bottom support remain readable at 1x across the entire bridge path, not only at one camera position.

findings.title: Wide reveal coverage
findings.observation: The overview has brighter output decks and weaker input/gantry separation. The black surrounding void makes the boundary pronounced.
findings.proposal: Trial broad low-level perimeter/gantry separation and redistribute plant coverage. Preserve the dark background if desired; do not brighten empty space or use depth of field as a lighting substitute.
findings.acceptance: Input, processing and output remain identifiable across the full orbit, with no exposure pumping or abrupt light activation.

finalSimulationCarryForward.target: the final agreed native simulation; greenfield_37 is currently an unvalidated reference
finalSimulationCarryForward.method: Re-anchor semantic zones to final actor bounds and review camera paths; do not copy old absolute positions blindly.
newZonesNotYetObservedInThisFilm: dock platform and truck cargo interior
constraints: Preserve the native simulation clock, actor poses, physical-video profile and insertion holds.
Keep brick colors and producer groups/scores unchanged.
Keep exposure consistent; try local fill before a global exposure increase.
No product UI or visible studio-light geometry.
Any animated light adjustment must be continuous across camera transitions and parallel-render boundaries.
Lighting is presentation support, not evidence of validated physical inspection performance.
reviewProcedure: Capture baseline and candidate at identical simulation times, poses, cameras, exposure and encoding settings.
Review P1 zones first at 4K and presentation-size 1080p.
Compare both holds, the complete bridge journey and the final full orbit.
Check bright bars and rollers, shadow detail, temporal stability and four-GPU boundary consistency.
Approve candidate stills and short previews before rendering a full replacement film.
